prediction:
THOUGHT: A 58-year-old man with a 3-month, painless, nonhealing ulcer at the vermillion border of the lower lip has multiple risk factors for lip cancer: male sex, age >50, a 20 pack-year smoking history, and prolonged occupational sun exposure as an outdoor fruit picker (actinic damage). The lower lip is the most common site for lip malignancies related to sun exposure. The lesion’s chronicity and lack of healing are concerning for malignancy. The biopsy shows dysplasia and keratin pearls, histologic features characteristic of invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Other causes of a chronic lip ulcer (actinic cheilitis, traumatic ulcer, chronic infection, basal cell carcinoma) are less likely given the histopathology. Therefore the clinical picture plus confirmatory biopsy supports a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the lower lip.

DIAGNOSIS: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lower lip (vermilion border).
